meaning: Scoring a policy on recorded frames by comparing the action it predicts with the recorded action; the policy's own actions never change what it sees next.
Letting the policy drive, on the bench, in a simulator or in a world model, so that each of its actions decides what it sees next, and counting successes.
The average squared distance between the policy's predicted action and the recorded action over the frames of a recording.
One complete run of a policy from the starting pose until the task succeeds, fails or runs out of time; also called a trial or an episode.
The number of rollouts that ended with the task done, divided by the number of rollouts.
A number between -1 and 1 that says how closely two lists of numbers rise and fall together; 1 means one predicts the other exactly, 0 means no relation.
Whether two ways of scoring put a set of policies in the same order; the Spearman correlation measures it by applying the Pearson calculation to rank positions.
A fixed set of simulated tasks that everyone scores on, so results can be compared.
The state of a benchmark on which nearly every policy scores near the top, so the score no longer separates good policies from poor ones.
The range of true success rates that would plausibly give the count that was observed.
One recipe for a confidence interval on a success rate, which stays between 0% and 100% and holds at small trial counts; LeRobot's evaluation tool reports it.
A test that says how often two policies with the same true success rate would show a gap at least as large as the one observed.
Closed-loop scoring in which a video world model generates what the cameras would show after each action and a vision-language model judges the generated video.
A model that takes images and text as input; used here as the judge of a generated rollout.
A real-robot ranking of policies built from blind pairwise comparisons run at seven academic institutions; the reference that simulators and world models are compared with.
A suite of simulated manipulation tasks used as a benchmark, now saturated; LIBERO-Plus is a successor that varies the scene.

expansion: International Conference on Robotics and Automation
meaning: A robotics research conference; its 2026 REAL-I challenge report is cited for what open-loop error misses.
